text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein, visiting Germany, and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl reaffirm the link between peace and development in strengthening hopes for security.
- Iraqi Trade Minister Mohamed Mehdi Saleh says after talks with Jordanian counterpart that cooperation between the two countries will increase as a result of U.N. oil-for-food deal.

- Top source tells Ad-Dustour that Jordan is deeply worried by breaks in relations and lack of communication among Arab leaders and by the many challenges facing Arabs. In the last few weeks King Hussein spoke to Iraqi President Saddam Hussein, Kuwait's emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah and Sudan's President General Omar Hassan al-Bashir.
- Iraqi Trade Minister Saleh blames U.S. for blocking or delaying Jordanian contracts with Iraq under the oil-for-food deal.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti and Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour discuss preparations for King Hussein's visit to Morocco in next few days.

- Jordan's representative to Arab-Israeli multilateral talks on refugees says Jordan plans soon to raise the issue on a bilateral level with Israel after consultation with Palestinians on the final status talks.
- Engineers Union chief Leith Shubeilat says engineers are resolved to go on strike on Saturday if government continues to refuse their demands.
- King Hussein and Morocco's King Hassan will discuss the status of Jerusalem and final status talks with Israelis during the Jordanian monarch's visit to Morocco.
- Jordan has won contracts to sell Iraq vegetable oils, detergents and soaps worth $100 million under the oil-for-food deal, senior trade ministry official says.
- Omani and American investors have set up a $45 million fund to invest in Oman and Jordan, Omani official says.
- Three men sentenced to life imprisonment for unearthing land mines near Israeli border and plotting terrorist actions.
- EU team in Jordan for talks on economic cooperation. Forty million Ecus, second part of a 100 million Ecu assistance grant, to be given to Jordan in next few days.
- Jordanian political parties pledge their support for Sudan's unity and warn of conspiracy.
- Jordan's chief of royal court Awn Khasawneh chairs meeting of human rights experts at U.N. headquarters in Geneva.
